finding.claim: Broken access control in ban(): the admin check is bypassed because abort(403) raises an HTTPException that is caught by `except Exception` and only logged; execution continues to do_ban(uid). Any authenticated non-admin user can ban arbitrary users.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban accepts POST; uid is attacker-controlled
non-admin => abort(403) raises werkzeug HTTPException (subclass of Exception)
only logs a warning (also logs user name); does not re-raise or return
do_ban(uid) executes regardless and returns ok=True

finding.guards_checked: require_admin is correct in itself and is used properly in unban() (admin.py:26) without try/except; no other decorator, before_request hook, or middleware exists in the repo (single file) that would enforce admin on ban(). The try/except swallows the only guard.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 for non-admins, but in ban() the call at admin.py:17 is wrapped in try/except Exception (18-19) that swallows it. There is no decorator, before_request hook or other control, and admin.py is the only file.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:16-20, abort(403) raised by require_admin (line 11) is a werkzeug HTTPException, which is an Exception subclass. It is caught at line 18 and only logged at line 19, so do_ban(uid) at line 20 runs for any non-admin caller, unlike unban() at line 26, which doesn't catch it. Cited line numbers are off by one in places (abort is on line 11, not 10) and do_ban is a stub, but the logic holds.
